column5: source
column6: target

column5: After that, all we needed was {i}this{/i}.
column6: 在那之后，我们只需要{i}这个{/i}。

column5: He holds up a dagger. The same one he used from the coliseum.{w}\nStabbing it through his hand, that's when the true nature of the weapon was revealed.{w}\nRather than piercing his hand, the blade sunk into the handle of the dagger. It was a fake.
column6: 他举起一把匕首。正是他在竞技场用过的那把。{w}\n他把匕首刺向自己的手，武器的真实本质才显露出来。{w}\n刀刃没有刺穿他的手，而是缩进了匕首的握柄里。那是把假匕首。

column5: Along with some chaos, and acting, they'd believe the battle was over.\nThe chaos, of course, was the moment [firstname] used the blade.\nWe pushed you toward using it, so we could have our opportunity.
column6: 再加上一些混乱和演技，他们便会相信战斗已经结束。\n那场混乱，当然就是[firstname]使用刀刃的那一刻。\n我们推着你使用它，为的就是给自己创造机会。

column5: That's really all there is to it.\nNone of you could know until it was already over.\nIf information was leaked, everything would be for nothing.
column6: 事情其实就是这么简单。\n在一切结束之前，你们谁都不能知道。\n一旦消息泄露，所有努力都会付诸东流。

column5: You're free to come back to Alarinthia, but we might stay behind.\nIt was just in our best interest to get away before they figured things out.\nSo yeah — a new alliance, minimal casualties, and a great story.
column6: 你们尽可以自由回到阿拉林西亚，但我们也许会留在后面。\n趁他们还没想明白之前脱身，对我们最有利。\n所以没错——新的同盟，最小的伤亡，还有一段精彩的故事。

column5: I'd say this was an all around success, wouldn't you?
column6: 我得说这是一次全面的成功，你不觉得吗？

column5: Yeah! I can't believe we really pulled it off.\nI think this might just be my masterpiece.
column6: 是啊！我真不敢相信我们真的办到了。\n我觉得这说不定就是我的杰作。

column5: They wait in silence for our response.{w}\nBut their faces are beaming with pride.
column6: 他们沉默地等待着我们的回应。{w}\n但他们的脸上洋溢着自豪。

column5: It seemed like a simple enough plan, but it was definitely risky.{w}\nThe moment we set foot in the coliseum, they were in real danger.{w}\nBut that only shows off their resolve. They were willing to die for this.
column6: 这计划看似简单，却绝对冒险。{w}\n我们踏进竞技场的那一刻，他们就身处真正的危险之中。{w}\n但这恰恰彰显了他们的决心。他们愿意为此赴死。

column5: However, something feels off about this.{w}\nIt's all too perfect, too convenient. I'm not sure.
column6: 然而，我总觉得有哪里不对劲。{w}\n一切都太完美，太顺理成章了。我说不准。

column5: Ulric was willing to throw everything away...?{w}\nChanging Alarinthia was his dream — he always said so.{w}\nSiding with Pro, and dismissing his chance to do it, was odd.
column6: 乌尔里克竟然愿意抛弃一切……？{w}\n改变阿拉林西亚是他的梦想——他一直这么说。{w}\n站在普洛那边，放弃实现梦想的机会，这很奇怪。

column5: There was obviously a chance that I'd side with Vivien, but I didn't.{w}\nI'd have to talk to Ulric about it later. There {i}had{/i} to be more to this story.
column6: 显然我有可能会站在薇薇安那边，但我没有。{w}\n我之后得找乌尔里克谈谈。这个故事{i}肯定{/i}还有内情。

column5: Ulric was willing to throw everything away...?{w}\nI mean, I sided with Vivien, but that wasn't a guarantee.{w}\nHad I sided with Draycu, he'd lose his chance to change Alarinthia.
column6: 乌尔里克竟然愿意抛弃一切……？{w}\n我是说，我确实站在薇薇安那边，但那并非万无一失。{w}\n要是我站在德雷库那边，他就会失去改变阿拉林西亚的机会。

column5: There {i}had{/i} to be more to this story. Something they're not telling us.{w}\nI'd have to talk to them in private later on. Maybe they could confide in me.
column6: 这个故事{i}肯定{/i}还有别的内情。有些事他们没告诉我们。{w}\n我之后得私下跟他们谈谈。也许他们愿意向我吐露。

column5: But as it stood, I didn't really buy their tale.{w}\nWould they really risk their lives for a foreign alliance?{w}\nMy comrades seem to think so, and they shower them with praise.
column6: 但就目前而言，我并不太相信他们的说辞。{w}\n他们真的会为了一纸异国同盟而冒生命危险吗？{w}\n我的同伴们似乎深信不疑，对他们赞不绝口。

column5: That might be the coolest thing I've ever heard.\nI knew you were a swindler Pro, but this is crazy.\nYou're using your skill to shape Alestia's history.
column6: 这也许是我听过最酷的事了。\n我知道你是个骗子，普洛，但这太疯狂了。\n你在用自己的本事改写阿莱斯蒂亚的历史。

column5: And Ulric, I never knew you were so good at acting.\nYou really had me sold there. I almost can't believe it.\nIt felt like something was up, but to think it was {i}this{/i}...?
column6: 还有乌尔里克，我从不知道你这么会演戏。\n你真是把我骗得团团转。我几乎不敢相信。\n我感觉有点不对劲，但没想到居然是{i}这个{/i}……？

column5: Almost puts my strategizing to shame, I have to say.\nSo what's the next step...? Is it just smooth sailing, now?\nI imagine our chances of getting caught are pretty low.
column6: 不得不说，这几乎让我自愧不如。\n那下一步呢……？现在就一帆风顺了吗？\n我想我们被抓到的几率应该很低。

column5: You should probably tell Draycu what {i}really{/i} went down.\nI doubt he'd mind, and at least he wouldn't find out another way.\nIn the meantime, we need to have a word with our new {i}prisoner{/i}.
column6: 你最好告诉德雷库{i}真正{/i}发生了什么。\n我想他不会介意，至少这样他不会从别处得知。\n与此同时，我们得跟我们新的{i}囚犯{/i}谈谈。

column5: You should probably tell Vivien what {i}really{/i} went down.\nI doubt he'd mind, and at least he wouldn't find out another way.\nIn the meantime, we need to have a word with our new {i}prisoner{/i}.
column6: 你最好告诉薇薇安{i}真正{/i}发生了什么。\n我想她不会介意，至少这样她不会从别处得知。\n与此同时，我们得跟我们新的{i}囚犯{/i}谈谈。

column5: Right. I'll tell him while you do that, then.\nBut I think we've also earned some much needed rest.\nLet's take the day off, and meet back up here in the morning.
column6: 好。那你去谈的时候，我来告诉他。\n不过我觉得我们也该好好休息一下了。\n今天休整一天，明早在这里碰头。

column5: That is, if it's okay with you, [firstname]?
column6: 如果你没意见的话，[firstname]？

column5: I nod, and tell everybody that they're dismissed.{w}\nEverybody runs off, except for Ulric and Pro.{w}\nThey approach me, and they look anxious.
column6: 我点点头，告诉大家可以解散了。{w}\n所有人都跑开了，只有乌尔里克和普洛留下。{w}\n他们向我走来，神情焦虑。

column5: Sovy is in the brig, right...?\nI can't believe he surrendered — just like that.
column6: 索维在禁闭室里，对吧……？\n我简直不敢相信他就这么投降了——就这样。

column5: And I heard him say something about a mole...?\nLet's go talk with him, [firstname]. You deserve some answers.
column6: 我好像听到他说了什么内鬼……？\n我们去跟他谈谈吧，[firstname]。你理应得到答案。

column5: Yeah. Let Damek pamper Draycu for the time being.\nBut before we head to the brig, look behind us, [firstname].\nIt's starting to look like an impressive army, isn't it...?
column6: 对。暂时让达梅克去讨好德雷库吧。\n但在我们去禁闭室之前，回头看看，[firstname]。\n这阵容开始像一支了不起的军队了，不是吗……？

column5: Yeah. Let Damek pamper Vivien for the time being.\nBut before we head to the brig, look behind us, [firstname].\nIt's starting to look like an impressive army, isn't it...?
column6: 对。暂时让达梅克去讨好薇薇安吧。\n但在我们去禁闭室之前，回头看看，[firstname]。\n这阵容开始像一支了不起的军队了，不是吗……？

column5: I do as instructed, and notice that we're accompanied by at least a dozen ships.{w}\nIf that was the strength of our new Alarinthian army, then I was at a loss for words.{w}\nThat fleet, combined with our own, and my blade, stood a real chance in Balteus.
column6: 我依言照做，发现至少有十几艘船与我们同行。{w}\n如果这就是我们新阿拉林西亚军队的实力，那我真是无话可说了。{w}\n那支舰队，加上我们自己的船队，还有我的刀刃，在巴尔泰乌斯确实有一战之力。

column5: But I couldn't lull myself into a false sense of security. There was still so much to do.{w}\nAnd right now, the next step was having a word with Sovy. Just what was he after...?{w}\nThe fact that Ulric and Pro \"volunteered\" to come along was also pretty peculiar.
column6: 但我不能让自己沉溺于虚假的安全感中。还有太多事要做。{w}\n而眼下，下一步就是跟索维谈谈。他究竟想要什么……？{w}\n乌尔里克和普洛“主动”要跟来这件事，也相当蹊跷。

column5: The pieces have started to fall into place, but there's still quite a few gaps.{w}\nMaybe this \"information\" that Sovy promised would help me in some way.{w}\nWe all head down to the brig, and I'm hopeful that I could figure this all out.
column6: 拼图开始各归其位，但仍有许多空白。{w}\n也许索维承诺的这个“情报”能以某种方式帮到我。{w}\n我们一起下到禁闭室，我希望能把这一切都弄清楚。

column5: After all, I could leave no question unanswered before attacking Balteus.{w}\nAnd resting in our brig was the one man who knew {i}everything{/i} about our enemy.{w}\nIf we could use him for information, then that would be an incredible boon.
column6: 毕竟，在进攻巴尔泰乌斯之前，我不能留下任何未解之谜。{w}\n而关在我们禁闭室里的，正是那个对我们敌人{i}无所不知{/i}的人。{w}\n如果我们能从他那里获取情报，那将是莫大的助力。

column5: As we enter the brig, one fact plays on repeat in my ever-running mind.
column6: 我们走进禁闭室时，一个念头在我永不停歇的脑海中反复回响。

column5: With everything we just gained? We actually stand a chance at winning this war...
column6: 有了我们刚刚得到的一切？我们真的有机会赢得这场战争了……

column5: The brig is dark, and we can't see much at all.{w}\nThat is, until our eyes adjust, and we immediately see Sovy.{w}\nHe's broken free from his binds, and is doing pull-ups from a ceiling beam.
column6: 禁闭室里一片漆黑，我们几乎什么都看不见。{w}\n直到眼睛适应过来，我们立刻看到了索维。{w}\n他挣脱了束缚，正吊在天花板的横梁上做引体向上。

column5: Grunting with exertion, he lets himself fall to the ground when he notices our entrance.{w}\nTaking a few steps toward us, he's careful not to make any sudden movements.{w}\nPro makes sure the cell door is shut and locked, so he can't escape from us.
column6: 他吃力地闷哼着，注意到我们进来后便松手落到地上。{w}\n他朝我们走了几步，小心翼翼地不做出任何突然的动作。{w}\n普洛确认牢房门已关好上锁，这样他就无法从我们手里逃走。

column5: My, my. I wasn't expecting an entourage.\nShould I be flattered, or concerned for my safety?
column6: 哎呀呀。我可没料到会来这么一大群人。\n我该感到受宠若惊，还是该担心自己的安危呢？

column5: An obvious attempt at humor, but none of us acknowledge this.{w}\nUlric steps forward, demanding swift answers from our captive.
column6: 这明显是想开个玩笑，但我们谁都没理会。{w}\n乌尔里克上前一步，要求我们的俘虏立刻给出答案。

column5: Explain yourself, Sovy.\nI'm seconds away from throwing you overboard.
column6: 解释清楚，索维。\n我随时都能把你扔下船。

column5: Again with the hostility.\nLook, I don't even really know what I'm doing here.\nIt just felt like the right thing to do, given the circumstances.
column6: 又是这种敌意。\n听着，我其实都不太清楚自己为什么会在这里。\n只是在那种情况下，这么做感觉是对的。

column5: What circumstances...?
column6: 什么情况……？

column5: Sovy looks at me, and shakes his head dismissively.
column6: 索维看了我一眼，不以为然地摇了摇头。

column5: Back when we attacked your HQ in Mazeo?\nMy goal was to kill your friend, and retrieve the blade.\nI failed both objectives, and The Triumvirate punished me.
column6: 还记得我们袭击你们在马泽奥的总部那次吗？\n我的目标是杀了你的朋友，取回刀刃。\n我两个目标都失败了，三人执政团因此惩罚了我。

column5: I see.
column6: 原来如此。

column5: It's true. Sovy did show me mercy during our brief encounter.{w}\nHe had my life in his hands, but he chose to run away instead.{w}\nHe saw something when he touched the blade — I could tell.
column6: 这是真的。在那次短暂的交锋中，索维确实对我手下留情了。{w}\n我的命就攥在他手里，可他却选择逃走。{w}\n他触碰刀刃时看到了什么——我能看出来。

column5: And now that I know the truth of the spirit realm, I think I knew what he saw.{w}\nThe Monarchy. He must've seen the same truth that shocked all of us.{w}\nI ask if that's true, almost certain that I'm correct. He then confirms.
column6: 如今既然我知道了灵界的真相，我想我明白他看到的是什么了。{w}\n王室。他一定看到了那个震撼我们所有人的真相。{w}\n我问他是不是这样，几乎确信自己是对的。随后他证实了。

column5: You are correct. I found out that The Triumvirate was lying to me.\nI let you live, because I wasn't sure of what to do next. I'm still uncertain.\nWhen I got back to Balteus, they punished me by placing me in exile.
column6: 你说得对。我发现三人执政团一直在骗我。\n我放你一命，是因为我不确定接下来该怎么做。我至今仍不确定。\n我回到巴尔泰乌斯后，他们把我流放，以此惩罚我。

column5: You expect us to believe this...?\nSovy, you're nothing but a mindless slave.\nThe Monarch survived because of his strength.
column6: 你以为我们会相信这种鬼话……？\n索维，你不过是个没有思想的奴隶。\n君主能活下来，靠的是他的力量。

column5: You expect us to believe this...?\nSovy, you're nothing but a mindless slave.\nThe Monarch survived because of her strength.
column6: 你以为我们会相信这种鬼话……？\n索维，你不过是个没有思想的奴隶。\n君主能活下来，靠的是她的力量。

column5: I tell Ulric that Sovy is speaking the truth.{w}\nI explain what happened while we were alone near the idol.
column6: 我告诉乌尔里克，索维说的是实话。{w}\n我解释了我们在灵像附近独处时发生的事。

column5: See, Ulric? You're always so paranoid.\nListen to your friends before making snap judgments.\nI have a lot to say, so you better learn to trust me again.
column6: 看到了吗，乌尔里克？你总是这么多疑。\n下结论之前先听听朋友的话。\n我有很多话要说，所以你最好学会重新信任我。

column5: Don't count on it.
column6: 别指望。

column5: He walks away and stands in a nearby corner.{w}\nSensing an opportunity, Pro enters the conversation.
column6: 他走开，站到旁边的角落里。{w}\n普洛察觉到机会，加入了谈话。

column5: So what did you want to tell us...?\nAround here, you need to earn your keep.\nUlric was serious about throwing you overboard.
column6: 那你想告诉我们什么……？\n在这里，你得自己挣得立足之地。\n乌尔里克说把你扔下船可不是开玩笑的。

column5: Well, this is where it gets complicated.\nI still consider myself a servant to The Triumvirate.\nBut Halin...? Well, I want nothing more than to see him fall.
column6: 好吧，事情到这里就复杂了。\n我仍然把自己视为三人执政团的仆人。\n但哈林……？我最大的心愿就是看他倒台。

column5: I'm not here to hurt any of you. Not this time.\nAs you can see, even though I broke out of my binds, I am playing nice.\nRight now, all I can offer is information to aid your attack on Balteus.
column6: 我不是来伤害你们任何人的。这次不是。\n如你所见，虽然我挣脱了束缚，但我很守规矩。\n眼下，我能提供的只有协助你们进攻巴尔泰乌斯的情报。

column5: And why would you want to help us take down The Triumvirate...?
column6: 那你为什么想帮我们扳倒三人执政团……？

column5: Doing so would involve taking down Halin, as well.\nHe sold me out, and got me into this whole mess.
column6: 这么做同时也意味着扳倒哈林。\n是他出卖了我，把我卷进了这摊浑水。

column5: Okay, and let's say we take down Halin. What then?\nYou'd be reinstated as Inquisitor, and just stab us in the back.
column6: 好，那就假设我们扳倒了哈林。然后呢？\n你会官复原职当回审判官，然后反手捅我们一刀。

column5: You speak as if people aren't capable of playing both sides.\nEither way, I don't know. I'd make my choice when the time comes.
column6: 你说得好像人就不能两面兼顾似的。\n不管怎样，我不知道。等时机到了我自会做出选择。

column5: And what makes you say that so easily...?\nYou've served The Triumvirate for your entire life.
column6: 那你怎么能这么轻松地说出这种话……？\n你为三人执政团效力了一辈子。

column5: No. Not my entire life.\nThey welcomed me with open arms, when I was young, and broken.\nNow here they are, inflicting the same wounds they had promised to heal.
column6: 不。不是一辈子。\n在我年幼又破碎的时候，他们张开双臂接纳了我。\n而如今，他们却在制造那些他们曾承诺要治愈的伤口。

column5: Is that supposed to make sense to me?
column6: 这话我该听懂吗？

column5: No, because it barely makes sense to {i}me{/i}.\nNow Pro, will you let me say what I have to say?
column6: 不，因为连{i}我{/i}自己都几乎理不清。\n好了普洛，你能让我把要说的话说完吗？

column5: Sure.
column6: 行。

column5: Sovy sighs, and crosses his arms.
column6: 索维叹了口气，抱起双臂。

column5: If you want to take down The Triumvirate, you'll have to enter their chambers.\nI've never seen them leave, and I don't expect that they ever will.\nI always thought they were hiding, but I don't think that's true.
column6: 如果你想扳倒三人执政团，就必须进入他们的内殿。\n我从没见过他们离开那里，也不认为他们会有离开的一天。\n我一直以为他们是在躲藏，但我觉得并非如此。

column5: There's something at the back of their chambers. Something \"off\".\nIt's like a spirit idol, but the very sight of it fills me with fear.\nI'm not sure what it is, but I have a few theories about it.
column6: 他们内殿的深处有样东西。有些“不对劲”。\n它像是灵界灵像，但我光是看到它就满心恐惧。\n我不确定它是什么，但我有几个猜测。

column5: I'm shocked. He's actually telling the truth.{w}\nI've seen this \"idol\" in my visions of The Triumvirate.{w}\nCould it really be true? Is he doubting his Masters...?
column6: 我震惊了。他居然说的是实话。{w}\n我在关于三人执政团的幻象里见过这座“灵像”。{w}\n这难道是真的？他是在怀疑他的主人吗……？

column5: I think that maybe it's their source of power.\nBut I'm probably wrong, as that seems to be the trend lately.\nEither way, its destruction should be your top priority.
column6: 我觉得那也许是他们力量的源泉。\n但我大概猜错了，最近似乎总是这样。\n不管怎样，摧毁它应该是你们的头等大事。

column5: It lines up with what I was told in my visions.{w}\nBut I was unsure if those visions were tricks.{w}\nIn them, I was drawn toward this special \"idol\".
column6: 这与我幻象中被告知的内容吻合。{w}\n但我当时不确定那些幻象是不是骗局。{w}\n在幻象里，我被这座特殊的“灵像”所吸引。

column5: A spirit idol in their own chambers...?\nBut those are conduits for The Monarchy.\nIt makes no sense that they'd keep one close by.
column6: 在他们自己的内殿里放一座灵界灵像……？\n可那些是王室的媒介。\n他们把它留在身边，这完全说不通。

column5: Their main goal was to {i}destroy{/i} all of the idols.\nNice try, but I'm not going to believe any of this.\nLet's go, [firstname]. We'll ditch him in Mazeo.
column6: 他们的主要目标就是{i}摧毁{/i}所有灵像。\n想得美，这些我一个字都不信。\n我们走，[firstname]。到马泽奥就把他甩掉。

column5: Pro and Ulric start to leave, but I tell them to stop.{w}\nI let them know that Sovy's telling the truth. As odd as it sounded.{w}\nI saw the same idol in some visions I had of The Triumvirate's chambers.
column6: 普洛和乌尔里克正要离开，但我叫住了他们。{w}\n我告诉他们，索维说的是实话，尽管听起来很古怪。{w}\n在我关于三人执政团内殿的几次幻象中，我见过同一座灵像。

column5: Visions of The Triumvirate's chambers...?
column6: 三人执政团内殿的幻象……？

column5: When were you going to tell us about this...?
column6: 你打算什么时候才告诉我们这些……？

column5: Sovy scoffs, clearly amused at their reactions.
column6: 索维嗤笑一声，显然被他们的反应逗乐了。

column5: I'm not finished yet.
column6: 我还没说完。

column5: Our attention is directed back toward him.
column6: 我们的注意力又回到了他身上。

column5: I suggest that your attack focuses on entering their chambers.\nThere, you could take down both them, and this \"dark idol\".\nHowever, you would have to fight your way through Halin.
column6: 我建议你们的进攻重点放在进入他们的内殿上。\n在那里，你们既能扳倒他们，也能摧毁这座“黑暗灵像”。\n但你们必须一路杀过哈林才行。

column5: And that's where my next piece of information comes in.\nHalin may seem just like you and I — but he's not.\nThe Triumvirate created him with that blade.
column6: 而这就是我下一条情报的由来。\n哈林看起来和你我没什么两样——但他不是。\n三人执政团用那把刀刃创造了他。

column5: What...?
column6: 什么……？

column5: He was made to be the perfect soldier.\nHe would always serve his Masters, no matter what.\nLittle did I know, that loyalty was stronger than our friendship.
column6: 他被造出来，就是要成为完美的士兵。\n无论发生什么，他都会效忠他的主人。\n我那时候并不知道，那份忠诚比我们的友谊还要牢固。

column5: He promised not to tell them what happened.\nBut the moment we got home, he sold me out immediately.\nHe lives under The Triumvirate's thrall. A {i}true{/i} mindless slave.
column6: 他答应过不告诉他们发生了什么。\n但我们一到家，他就立刻出卖了我。\n他活在三人执政团的奴役之下。一个{i}真正{/i}没有思想的奴隶。

column5: You must never let them get their hands on that blade again.\nThey aren't limited to suits of armor. They've mastered it enough to create {i}life{/i}.\nOf course, their first test was Halin. They needed someone trustworthy enough to serve them.
column6: 你们绝不能让他们再次拿到那把刀刃。\n他们的造物不限于盔甲。他们已经精通到足以创造{i}生命{/i}。\n当然，他们的第一个试验品就是哈林。他们需要一个足够可靠的人来服侍他们。

column5: I think they did it to ensure that nobody else ran away.\nMy previous Master, the former Grand Inquisitor, defected.\nI trusted Halin, {i}and{/i} The Triumvirate. They all betrayed me.
column6: 我猜他们这么做，是为了确保再没有别人会逃走。\n我前一任主人，前任大审判官，叛逃了。\n我信任哈林，{i}也{/i}信任三人执政团。他们全都背叛了我。

column5: But there's your information. I'm sure it will help you out.\nA possible weakness, and the true nature of Halin.\nWith that blade, you could even give him freedom.
column6: 但这就是我给你们的的情报。我相信它会帮上你们的忙。\n一个可能的弱点，以及哈林的真实本质。\n有了那把刀刃，你们甚至可以赐予他自由。

column5: It would release the spell that The Triumvirate has put on him.\nOf course, that's not how I'd like things to play out.
column6: 那会解除三人执政团施加在他身上的咒术。\n当然，我并不希望事情朝那个方向发展。

column5: He smirks at me, and I can sense what he's about to say.
column6: 他朝我笑了笑，我能感觉到他接下来要说什么。

column5: I would prefer it if you let me kill him, [firstname].\nThat is all I ask for in return. I {i}won't{/i} get in your way.\nIf you grant me this, I would be further in your debt.
column6: 我更希望你能让我杀了他，[firstname]。\n这就是我索要的全部回报。我{i}不会{/i}妨碍你们。\n如果你答应我，我会欠你更多人情。

column5: We all look at each other, slightly confused.{w}\nThe Triumvirate created Halin to be a perfect slave?{w}\nI guess it makes sense, especially if they dealt with defection.
column6: 我们面面相觑，有些困惑。{w}\n三人执政团为了造出完美的奴隶才创造了哈林？{w}\n我想这说得通，尤其是考虑到他们要对付叛逃问题。

column5: But just what was this idol at the back of their chambers...?{w}\nAnd was destroying it really the best course of action?{w}\nI guess we wouldn't find out until the very end of things.
column6: 可他们内殿深处的那座灵像到底是什么……？{w}\n摧毁它真的是最好的做法吗？{w}\n我想我们得等到最后才能揭晓了。

column5: So, do you trust me...?
column6: 那么，你们信任我吗……？

column5: We all nod reluctantly. These facts weren't revelations, but they helped.{w}\nIf I could free Halin, he might end up being a valuable asset.{w}\nHowever, the idol remained a true wild card in all of this.
column6: 我们都勉强点了点头。这些事实算不上新发现，但有帮助。{w}\n如果我能解放哈林，他也许会成为一个宝贵的战力。{w}\n然而，那座灵像始终是这一切中真正的变数。

column5: If I ever got the chance to talk to The Triumvirate, I'd ask them.{w}\nBut something tells me, if we're face to face, it won't be civil.{w}\nAnd for all I know, it's just a trick. The idol could be a red herring.
column6: 要是我有机会跟三人执政团谈谈，我会问问他们。{w}\n但直觉告诉我，真到了面对面的时候，可不会是什么文明的对话。{w}\n而且说不定这根本就是个圈套。那座灵像也许只是障眼法。

column5: Good. Because there's {i}two{/i} more things to talk about.\nAnd now that I've earned your trust, you have {i}no{/i} reason to doubt them.\nI saved them for last, because, well — it involves dishonesty among your ranks.
column6: 很好。因为还有{i}两{/i}件事要谈。\n既然我已经赢得了你们的信任，你们就{i}没有{/i}理由怀疑它们了。\n我把它们留到最后，因为，嗯——这涉及到你们队伍里的不诚实行为。

column5: It must be about that mole he mentioned...{w}\nI tell him to quit dancing around the subject, and tell me.{w}\nWe had a lot of planning to do for our final attack, and very little time.
column6: 一定是他提到过的那个内鬼……{w}\n我叫他别再绕圈子，直接告诉我。{w}\n我们为最后的进攻还有很多要筹划的，时间却很少。

column5: Well then. Do {i}you{/i} two want to tell him, or should I...?
column6: 那好吧。{i}你们{/i}两个想自己告诉他，还是我来……？

column5: Well then. Do {i}you{/i} two want to tell her, or should I...?
column6: 那好吧。{i}你们{/i}两个想自己告诉她，还是我来……？

column5: Pro and Ulric shuffle in silence, clearly in a state of unease.{w}\nWhat was Sovy talking about...? There's no way Ulric and Pro were dishonest.{w}\nThey had served Damek and Salus for decades. They were easily the most trustworthy.
column6: 普洛和乌尔里克一言不发，局促地挪动着，显然很不安。{w}\n索维在说什么……？乌尔里克和普洛绝不可能不诚实。{w}\n他们为达梅克和萨卢斯效力了几十年。他们无疑是最值得信赖的人。

column5: I guess it's time. I'll go first.
column6: 看来是时候了。我先说。

column5: Ulric steps forward, taking a deep breath.{w}\nSovy watches with his signature smirk.
column6: 乌尔里克上前一步，深吸一口气。{w}\n索维带着他标志性的坏笑看着。

column5: My allegiance is with The Rebellion, I can promise you that.\nBut that wasn't always the case. It's all in the past — ages ago.\nSovy is trying to harm our trust with ancient information, [firstname].
column6: 我可以向你保证，我效忠的是反抗军。\n但并非一直如此。那都是过去的事了——很久很久以前。\n索维想用陈年旧事来破坏我们的信任，[firstname]。

column5: I knew this was going to happen. \nHe'd earn your trust with a couple interesting facts, then attack.\nThis is subterfuge. My past has no bearing on my current loyalty.
column6: 我就知道会这样。\n他会用几个有趣的事实赢得你的信任，然后发动攻击。\n这是诡计。我的过去与我如今的忠诚毫无关系。

column5: But I knew this secret would come out sooner or later.\nThat's the {i}real{/i} reason I sided with Pro to cheat the coliseum.\nYou'd know my loyalty was with you — no matter what.
column6: 但我知道这个秘密迟早会暴露。\n这才是我和普洛联手在竞技场作弊的{i}真正{/i}原因。\n这样你就会知道，无论发生什么，我的忠诚都在你这边。

column5: That much is true. He had no guarantee that I'd side with Vivien.{w}\nHe threw away his beliefs in order to help {i}me{/i} achieve his goal.{w}\nThat was proof enough of his loyalty. But I'm still a bit concerned.
column6: 这话没错。他无法保证我会站在薇薇安那边。{w}\n为了帮我{i}自己{/i}实现他的目标，他抛弃了自己的信念。{w}\n这已足够证明他的忠诚。但我还是有点担心。

column5: That much is true. He had no guarantee that I'd side with Vivien.{w}\nHe didn't have to, in the end — but he was willing to abandon his dreams.{w}\nThat was proof enough of his loyalty. But I was still a bit concerned.
column6: 这话没错。他无法保证我会站在薇薇安那边。{w}\n到头来他本不必如此——但他愿意抛弃自己的梦想。{w}\n这已足够证明他的忠诚。但我还是有点担心。

column5: Delaying, as always.\nHe's scared of you, [firstname].\nHe knows you might throw him away.
column6: 一如既往地拖延。\n他怕你，[firstname]。\n他知道你可能会抛弃他。

column5: No. [firstname] would never do that.\nNot after what I did for our cause in Alarinthia.\nSo go ahead, Sovy, watch your plan crumble and fall.
column6: 不。[firstname]绝不会那么做。\n尤其在我为我们在阿拉林西亚的事业做了那些事之后。\n所以尽管来吧，索维，看着你的计划土崩瓦解。

column5: I notice a weight lift itself from my back.{w}\nThe blade disappears from my scabbard. Sovy is doing it again...!{w}\nHowever, much to my surprise — that's not what happens next.
column6: 我感觉到一股压力从背上卸下。{w}\n刀刃从我的剑鞘里消失了。索维又要故技重施……！{w}\n然而，出乎我意料的是——接下来发生的并非如此。

column5: Ulric sighs, in both relief and fright, as the blade appears in his hands.{w}\nI take a few steps back, shocked. How in the world was this possible...!?
column6: 刀刃出现在乌尔里克手中，他松了口气，却又满怀惊惧。{w}\n我震惊地后退了几步。这到底怎么可能……！？

column5: Grand Inquisitor Ulric...\nThat was lifetimes ago. Ancient history.\nHe's using a dead past to try and hurt us, [firstname].
column6: 大审判官乌尔里克……\n那是好几辈子以前的事了。是古老的历史。\n他想用一个已死的过去来伤害我们，[firstname]。

column5: Ulric was a Grand Inquisitor...?{w}\nThen he must be the defector that Sovy mentioned.{w}\nThe pieces of all of this are starting to fall into place!
column6: 乌尔里克曾是大审判官……？{w}\n那他一定就是索维提到的那个叛逃者。{w}\n这一切的拼图开始各归其位了！

column5: I realized that The Triumvirate was my true enemy.\nThat's when I decided to join The Rebellion.\nYou really thought this would work, Sovy...?
column6: 我意识到三人执政团才是我真正的敌人。\n那时我决定加入反抗军。\n你真以为这招会奏效吗，索维……？

column5: I never said I was intending to hurt you.\nThis is merely information that might help you in Balteus.\nUlric has inside knowledge, [firstname] — and he can wield the blade.
column6: 我从没说过我打算伤害你。\n这只是一条或许能在巴尔泰乌斯帮到你们的情报。\n乌尔里克掌握着内部情报，[firstname]——而且他能使用刀刃。

column5: It's your choice if you let this information hurt you.\nBut in your situation, I would be relieved to know.\nNow, there's no need to keep anymore secrets.
column6: 是否让这条情报伤到你，取决于你。\n但换作是我处在你这种境地，知道这些反而会松一口气。\n现在，没必要再保留任何秘密了。

column5: Hmph.
column6: 哼。

column5: I'm so confused right now. Was Sovy helping us, or trying to hurt us?{w}\nI can see how he might think that Ulric's past would harm our trust.{w}\nBut I can also see how sharing this information would help us out.
column6: 我现在糊涂极了。索维是在帮我们，还是想害我们？{w}\n我能理解他为什么会觉得乌尔里克的过去会损害我们的信任。{w}\n但我也能看出，分享这条情报会帮到我们。

column5: Furthermore, the way Ulric handled this situation was extremely professional.{w}\nUnder any other circumstances, I might have taken this information badly.{w}\nBut he's right. It's in the past. He's gone on to prove his loyalty to me.
column6: 而且，乌尔里克处理这件事的方式极为专业。{w}\n换作其他任何情况，我可能会对这条情报反应激烈。{w}\n但他说得对。那都是过去的事了。他已经用行动证明了对我的忠诚。

column5: The happenings in Alarinthia finally make full sense to me.{w}\nHe was securing my trust for when this secret came to light.{w}\nGenius, really. I'd have to deal with him more later on, though.
column6: 阿拉林西亚发生的一切终于让我完全明白了。{w}\n他是在为这个秘密曝光的那一天预先赢得我的信任。{w}\n真是天才。不过，我以后得跟他多打交道了。

column5: This conversation had potential to explode, and I'm glad that it didn't.{w}\nI know Ulric's real plan, but Pro still remains a wild card. What was he after...?{w}\nI turn to face him, and he takes that as a signal that it's his turn to talk.
column6: 这场谈话本有可能一触即发，幸好没有。{w}\n我明白了乌尔里克的真实打算，但普洛仍是个未知数。他想要什么……？{w}\n我转向他，他把这当作轮到他开口的信号。

column5: Ulric passes the blade back to me, and I place it in the scabbard.{w}\nPro looks worried. Perhaps his secret was worse than Ulric's...?
column6: 乌尔里克把刀刃递还给我，我将其插回剑鞘。{w}\n普洛看起来很担忧。也许他的秘密比乌尔里克的更糟糕……？

column5: Go on. Tell [firstname], Pro.\nIt's time for him to know, don't you think?
column6: 说吧。告诉[firstname]，普洛。\n是时候让他知道了，你不觉得吗？

column5: Go on. Tell [firstname], Pro.\nIt's time for her to know, don't you think?
column6: 说吧。告诉[firstname]，普洛。\n是时候让她知道了，你不觉得吗？

column5: He gulps before speaking.
column6: 他咽了口唾沫，才开口。

column5: So I guess I'll start from the beginning. My parents abandoned me.\nThey didn't die in the occupation, like I tell everybody.\nI've always wanted to know one thing — \"why\"...?
column6: 那我就从头说起吧。我的父母抛弃了我。\n他们不像我跟所有人说的那样，死在占领时期。\n我一直想知道一件事——“为什么”……？

column5: None of my searches gave me any useful information.\nSo, over time, I grew more and more desperate.\nOne day — The Triumvirate reached out to me.
column6: 我的所有搜寻都没能给我任何有用的信息。\n于是，随着时间推移，我变得越来越绝望。\n有一天——三人执政团主动联系了我。

column5: He looks down, ashamed.
column6: 他低下头，满脸羞愧。

column5: They said they knew the truth about my parents.\nBut in exchange, they wanted me to give them information.\nDetails about The Rebellion. It seemed like a harmless exchange.
column6: 他们说他们知道我父母的事真相。\n但作为交换，他们要我把情报交给他们。\n关于反抗军的细节。这看起来像是一场无害的交易。

column5: Pro was the mole...
column6: 普洛就是那个内鬼……

column5: But over time, they started to ask for more and more.\nI gave them so many secrets, but got nothing in return.\nIt wasn't much longer before I quit. I had enough of their lies.
column6: 但时间一长，他们开始索取越来越多。\n我给了他们那么多秘密，却什么回报都没得到。\n没过多久我就退出了。我受够了他们的谎言。

column5: But the damage was already done, wasn't it...?
column6: 但伤害已经造成了，不是吗……？

column5: Yeah...
column6: 是啊……

column5: What was the last thing you leaked to them, Pro?
column6: 你最后泄露给他们的是什么，普洛？

column5: The location of our new HQ. The tunnels.\nIt was a good hideout. Right under their noses.\nThey'd never find it, unless somebody told them.
column6: 我们新总部的所在地。那些地道。\n那是个很好的藏身处。就在他们眼皮底下。\n除非有人告诉他们，否则他们永远找不到。

column5: I'm shocked to my core.{w}\nIf Pro leaked our location, then that means...
column6: 我震惊到了骨子里。{w}\n如果普洛泄露了我们的位置，那就意味着……

column5: That's right. Pro is responsible.\nHis leak enabled us to attack you in Mazeo.\nAll of those lives. The blood is on {i}his{/i} hands.
column6: 没错。普洛难辞其咎。\n正是他的泄露让我们得以在马泽奥袭击你们。\n那些逝去的生命。血都沾在{i}他{/i}手上。

column5: No...! Like I said, I quit!\nThey lied to me. They knew {i}nothing{/i} about my parents.\nAll they wanted was somebody gullible enough to serve them.
column6: 不……！我说过了，我退出了！\n他们骗了我。他们对我的父母{i}一无所知{/i}。\n他们只是想要一个足够轻信的人来替他们卖命。

column5: It doesn't change what happened, Pro.\nNow, Monarch — how do you take this...?
column6: 这改变不了已经发生的事，普洛。\n那么，君主——你对此怎么看……？

column5: Hey, I proved my loyalty — just like Ulric!\nI put my life on the line to serve The Rebellion.\nThere was no guarantee we'd survive the coliseum!
column6: 嘿，我证明了我的忠诚——就像乌尔里克一样！\n我冒着生命危险为反抗军效力。\n我们在竞技场里可没有活下来的保证！

column5: That much was true. I knew everything was too good to be true.{w}\nThe {i}real{/i} reasons they did what they did, were all self-serving.{w}\nIt was so they could defend themselves as they were exposed.
column6: 这话没错。我早就知道一切都好得不像是真的。{w}\n他们那么做的{i}真正{/i}原因，全都是为了自己。{w}\n是为了在真相败露时能为自己辩解。

column5: With an ulterior motive like that, were they really trustworthy...?{w}\nUlric's past was easy to forgive. But what Pro did to all of us?{w}\nI have no idea how to react. Sovy was fighting a war on my mind.
column6: 怀着这样的私心，他们真的值得信赖吗……？{w}\n乌尔里克的过去容易原谅。可普洛对我们所有人做的事呢？{w}\n我完全不知道该如何反应。索维正在我的脑海中打一场仗。

column5: Look — I made up for what I did...!\nAll those lives we lost? We got them back, and more!\nOur Alarinthian allies will help us win this war. Hands down.
column6: 听着——我已经弥补了我做过的事……！\n我们失去的那些生命？我们不仅夺回来了，还得到了更多！\n我们的阿拉林西亚盟友会帮我们赢得这场战争。毫无疑问。

column5: I nod, acknowledging his point.{w}\nBut I need more time to think about this.{w}\nIf they had secrets, did my other comrades, too?
column6: 我点点头，承认他说得有道理。{w}\n但我需要更多时间来考虑这件事。{w}\n如果他们都有秘密，那我其他的同伴是不是也一样？

column5: I'm starting to doubt the loyalty of everybody around me.{w}\nI need to stop...! That's probably what Sovy wants me to do.{w}\nI'd need to ensure everyone's loyalty before we leave to Balteus.
column6: 我开始怀疑身边每个人的忠诚。{w}\n我得停下……！这大概正是索维希望我做的。{w}\n在出发去巴尔泰乌斯之前，我得确保每个人的忠诚。

column5: Ulric was the previous Grand Inquisitor...?{w}\nPro was a mole, responsible for the attack in Mazeo...?{w}\nHow was I supposed to deal with this, {i}right{/i} before the final battle?
column6: 乌尔里克是前任大审判官……？{w}\n普洛是内鬼，该为马泽奥的袭击负责……？{w}\n就在决战{i}前夕{/i}，我该如何应对这一切？

column5: I ask Ulric and Pro to leave me alone with Sovy.{w}\nWe'd get some rest, and meet on the deck in the morning.{w}\nOne big gathering before we arrived in Mazeo would help.
column6: 我让乌尔里克和普洛留我和索维单独待着。{w}\n我们会稍作休息，明早在甲板上碰头。{w}\n在抵达马泽奥之前来一次大聚会会有帮助。

column5: I can see the worry on their faces. I tell them I'm not \"throwing them away\".{w}\nAs they leave, the worry is still there, however. Their secrets were finally out.{w}\nI don't know if anybody else knew — but I guess I was enough. I'm in charge.
column6: 我能看到他们脸上的忧虑。我告诉他们，我不会“抛弃他们”。{w}\n然而，他们离开时，忧虑依旧还在。他们的秘密终究是暴露了。{w}\n我不知道还有没有别人知情——但我想，只有我知道就够了。做主的是我。

column5: I turn back to Sovy, who crosses his arms.
column6: 我转回索维那边，他抱着双臂。

column5: So much dishonesty in the air, wouldn't you agree...?\nI want you to look at your comrades, and then look at me.\nUnlike them — I've been nothing but honest with you.
column6: 空气中弥漫着这么多谎言，你不觉得吗……？\n我要你看看你的同伴们，然后再看看我。\n和他们不同——我对你一直坦诚相待。

column5: I would rather have an honest enemy than a cheating friend.\nThat's part of why I wanted to talk with you, [firstname].\nI know that we can be open with one another.
column6: 我宁愿要一个诚实的敌人，也不要一个欺骗人的朋友。\n这也是我想跟你谈谈的原因之一，[firstname]。\n我知道我们之间可以开诚布公。

column5: I shake my head, unsure of how to respond.{w}\nI tell him that I need some rest. Some time alone.{w}\nSo much was happening all at once. I needed a break.
column6: 我摇了摇头，不知该如何回应。{w}\n我告诉他我需要休息。需要独处一会儿。{w}\n太多事一下子全都涌来了。我需要喘口气。

column5: Very well. We're meeting on the deck come morning, then?\nI'll make sure to be on my best behavior. I respect you, Monarch.\nI always told myself that I'd serve the rightful rulers of this world.
column6: 好吧。那我们明早在甲板上见？\n我保证会表现得规规矩矩。我敬重你，君主。\n我一直告诉自己，要效忠于这个世界正当的统治者。

column5: It just seems like I was also lied to by The Triumvirate.\nJust like Ulric. Just like Pro. We're victims here — all of us.\nI may have realized it late, but was it {i}too{/i} late? I guess we'll see.
column6: 看来三人执政团也骗了我。\n就像乌尔里克一样。就像普洛一样。我们都是受害者——我们所有人。\n我或许醒悟得太晚，但会不会{i}太{/i}晚了？我想我们走着瞧吧。

column5: His attitude seems to have changed now that we're alone.{w}\nAnd for the first time, I can sympathize with him. He's hurt, and lost.{w}\nJust like all of us. We're just trying to do what we believe is right.
column6: 既然只剩我们两个，他的态度似乎变了。{w}\n第一次，我对他生出了同情。他受了伤，也迷失了方向。{w}\n就像我们所有人一样。我们都只是在尽力做自己认为正确的事。

column5: I tell him that he's free to join us at the meeting in the morning.{w}\nBut everybody will be told who he is. It'll be up to them to decide how they take it.{w}\nIf the majority of my comrades want him gone, then we'll have to part ways in Mazeo.
column6: 我告诉他，他可以自由参加明早的会议。{w}\n但所有人都会知道他是谁。要怎么接受，就由他们自己决定。{w}\n如果我的大多数同伴希望他离开，那我们只能在马泽奥分道扬镳。

column5: Very well. It's only fair.\nHave a good rest, Monarch.
column6: 好吧。这才公平。\n好好休息，君主。

column5: He bows to me, as I turn to leave the cell.{w}\nI make sure it's locked tight. He'd be let out in the morning.{w}\nFor now, I needed to be alone with my thoughts. I needed to process everything.
column6: 我转身离开牢房时，他向我鞠了一躬。{w}\n我确认牢门锁得严严实实。明早会放他出来。{w}\n而现在，我需要独自理清思绪。我需要消化这一切。

column5: I make my way back to my bed, and quickly collapse onto it.{w}\nThe weight of recent events weighs me down like a ton of bricks.{w}\nAt the end of the day — I didn't know who I could really trust. It's awful.
column6: 我回到自己的床边，一下子瘫倒在上面。{w}\n近来发生的事像千斤重担一样压着我。{w}\n说到底——我根本不知道自己能真正信任谁。这感觉糟透了。

column5: Ulric and Pro, two of our most trusted comrades, had dark secrets.{w}\nIt makes me wonder just what everyone else was hiding. Even Valessa and Fortaime.{w}\nWhen we got back to Mazeo, I'd need to ensure their loyalty before we attacked Balteus.
column6: 乌尔里克和普洛，我们最信任的两位同伴，竟藏着黑暗的秘密。{w}\n这让我不禁去想，其他所有人又隐藏着什么。连瓦莱莎和福泰姆也不例外。{w}\n等我们回到马泽奥，在进攻巴尔泰乌斯之前，我得确保他们的忠诚。

column5: We couldn't embark on the biggest part of our journey with unresolved issues.{w}\nEverybody needed to be in tip-top shape. Not held down by anything at all.{w}\nAs big as Ulric and Pro's secrets were, it's information we didn't have before.
column6: 我们不能带着未解的隐患踏上旅途最重要的征程。{w}\n每个人都需要处于最佳状态。不被任何事情拖累。{w}\n无论乌尔里克和普洛的秘密多么重大，那也是我们此前所没有的情报。

column5: Information we could use against our enemy, and against Balteus.{w}\nWe were too close to our goal to fall apart due to internal politics.{w}\nI drift off to sleep, and make my way to the deck in the morning.
column6: 可以用来对付我们的敌人、对付巴尔泰乌斯的情报。{w}\n我们离目标太近了，不能因为内部分歧而分崩离析。{w}\n我沉沉睡去，第二天早晨来到了甲板上。

column5: It was time for everybody to know about Sovy.{w}\nThen, we'd have a final discussion about what comes next.{w}\nWe were ready to launch our attack. But what should we do...?
column6: 是时候让所有人都知道索维的事了。{w}\n之后，我们会就下一步进行最后的讨论。{w}\n我们已经准备好发动进攻。但我们该怎么做呢……？

column5: Everybody is standing there, as if they were waiting for me to arrive.{w}\nThey all exchange glances with Sovy, and unease fills the air.{w}\nI don't blame them for being reserved right now. Not at all.
column6: 所有人都站在那里，仿佛在等我到来。{w}\n他们纷纷与索维交换眼神，空气中弥漫着不安。{w}\n我不怪他们此刻的拘谨。一点也不。

column5: They all turn to face me, so that's when I hand the floor to Sovy.{w}\nIf he wanted to help us out, he had to win over my entire crew.{w}\nThe choice was with me, but all of their input was important.
column6: 他们全都转向我，于是我把发言权交给了索维。{w}\n如果他想帮我们，就必须赢得我所有手下的认可。{w}\n决定权在我，但所有人的意见都很重要。

column5: All of us gather around in a sort of \"circle\".{w}\nThis means he can easily address all of us.{w}\nI'm curious what he has to say. A lot is on the line.
column6: 我们所有人围成某种“圆圈”聚在一起。{w}\n这样他就能方便地对我们所有人讲话。{w}\n我很好奇他要说什么。事关重大。

column5: My name is Sovy. I am — or was — The Grand Inquisitor.\nI no longer serve The Triumvirate. I was betrayed by my Apprentice.\nHe sold me out, forcing my Masters to place me in exile. They threw me away.
column6: 我叫索维。我是——或者说曾是——大审判官。\n我不再效忠三人执政团了。我被我的学徒背叛了。\n他出卖了我，逼得我的主人把我流放。他们抛弃了我。

column5: Everything they ever told me was a lie. I thought they were Alestia's rightful rulers.\nBut then I figured out that this wasn't true. The heir to the throne is [firstname].\nI am a victim of their tyranny. Just as you are. All of you. I hope you understand.
column6: 他们告诉我的一切都是谎言。我本以为他们是阿莱斯蒂亚正当的统治者。\n但后来我明白了，事实并非如此。王位的继承人是[firstname]。\n我是他们暴政的受害者。就像你们一样。你们所有人。希望你们能明白。

column5: I'm still at a loss. I don't really know what to do with myself.\nBut coming here, to meet with you, and [firstname], seemed like a good idea.\nLast night, I also revealed some information that could help your upcoming attack.
column6: 我仍茫然无措。我真不知道拿自己该怎么办。\n但来到这里，与你们和[firstname]见面，似乎是个好主意。\n昨晚，我还透露了一些能帮到你们即将到来的进攻的情报。

column5: I just need to know that I {i}belong{/i} somewhere.\nAttacking The Triumvirate will involve taking down Halin.\nWe share a common purpose, at least until he's taken care of.
column6: 我只需要知道自己{i}属于{/i}某个地方。\n进攻三人执政团就意味着要扳倒哈林。\n我们有着共同的目标，至少在解决掉他之前是如此。

column5: After that? I really don't know.\nI've always pledged my loyalty to the rightful ruler of Alestia.\nLogic would dictate that I now serve The Monarch. But I don't know.
column6: 那之后呢？我真的不知道。\n我一直都向阿莱斯蒂亚正当的统治者宣誓效忠。\n照理说，我现在该效忠君主。但我不知道。

column5: The Triumvirate can throw people away at the snap of a finger.\nBut I'm not like that. What they did was hurt me almost beyond repair.\nI will help you attack Balteus, and take down Halin. You have my word.
column6: 三人执政团弹指之间就能抛弃一个人。\n但我不是那样的人。他们的所作所为几乎把我伤得无法复原。\n我会帮你们进攻巴尔泰乌斯，扳倒哈林。我向你们保证。

column5: But after that, I don't know what will happen.\nIn that sense, I am both an asset and a liability.\nIf you want me to leave — then that's what I'll do.
column6: 但那之后，我不知道会发生什么。\n从这个意义上说，我既是助力，也是隐患。\n如果你想让我离开——那我就离开。

column5: When we get to Mazeo, you'll never see me again.\nThat is, unless, you want my help. I can offer valuable intel.\nIt's a gamble, for both you {i}and{/i} me. I don't fully trust you, either.
column6: 等我们到马泽奥，你们就再也见不到我了。\n除非你们想要我的帮助。我能提供有价值的情报。\n这是一场赌博，对你们{i}和{/i}我都是。我也不完全信任你们。

column5: But hopefully I've earned a sliver of trust with [firstname].\nIf he vouches for me, then hopfully you will as well. That is all.\nMy fate is in your hands. I have nothing more to say.
column6: 但希望我已经赢得了[firstname]的一丝信任。\n如果他为我担保，那希望你们也会。就这些。\n我的命运掌握在你们手中。我没有别的要说了。

column5: But hopefully I've earned a sliver of trust with [firstname].\nIf she vouches for me, then hopefully you will as well. That is all.\nMy fate is in your hands. I have nothing more to say.
column6: 但希望我已经赢得了[firstname]的一丝信任。\n如果她为我担保，那希望你们也会。就这些。\n我的命运掌握在你们手中。我没有别的要说了。

column5: He crosses his arms, waiting for our reply.{w}\nMy comrades are all shocked and confused, save for Pro and Ulric.{w}\nI ask them to step forward, one by one, and offer their thoughts on this.
column6: 他抱着双臂，等待我们的答复。{w}\n除了普洛和乌尔里克，我的同伴们都又惊又惑。{w}\n我让他们一个一个上前，说说自己的想法。

column5: For once, I have the grasp on an entire situation.{w}\nThis is how things should be. Like Sovy said, I was the rightful ruler.{w}\nI couldn't have people being dishonest, and plotting behind my back.
column6: 这一次，我终于掌控了整个局面。{w}\n事情本该如此。就像索维说的，我是正当的统治者。{w}\n我不能容忍有人不诚实，在背后算计我。

column5: I honestly didn't expect this. But nothing has been normal lately.\nI'm willing to give Sovy a chance. I did the same thing with Gryz.\nHis defection marked a turning point for our cause. A big one.
column6: 老实说，我没想到会这样。但最近也没什么正常的。\n我愿意给索维一个机会。我当初对格瑞兹也是如此。\n他的倒戈是我们事业的转折点。很重要的一次转折。

column5: If he can help us out, then I think we need to accept it.\nAnd if he turns against us, then he's easily outnumbered.\nThe potential benefits outweigh the potential risks.
column6: 如果他能帮到我们，那我觉得我们就该接受。\n而如果他背叛我们，他在人数上轻易就能被压制。\n潜在的收益大于潜在的风险。

column5: This is clearly a trap. We request that you deny his assistance.\nHe's alone now, but he won't be when we arrive in Balteus.\nIf we give him information, he'll turn on us once we get there.
column6: 这显然是个陷阱。我们请求你拒绝他的协助。\n他现在孤身一人，但等我们到巴尔泰乌斯时就不是了。\n如果我们把情报给他，一到那里他就会反咬我们一口。

column5: Surely we aren't the only one who thinks this way...?\nAn alliance with our enemy mere days before our attack?\nIt's too convenient. Sovy is playing us for a fool.
column6: 我们肯定不是唯一这么想的吧……？\n在进攻前几天与敌人结盟？\n太巧了。索维是在把我们当傻子耍。

column5: I'm with Howl on this one. We can't work with the enemy.\nThis is the man that killed you, and burned down Valinorth in your vision.\nI know it was a trick, but the man is the same. He's a trained killer.
column6: 这次我站豪尔这边。我们不能和敌人合作。\n在幻象里，就是这个人杀了你，烧毁了瓦利诺斯。\n我知道那是个骗局，但人还是同一个人。他是个训练有素的杀手。

column5: For that reason, I can't accept his offer.\nFortaime, you're with me, right...?
column6: 正因如此，我无法接受他的提议。\n福泰姆，你跟我一伙的，对吧……？

column5: I don't know, Valessa. I think everybody deserves a second chance.\nWe all had that \"moment\" when we turned against The Triumvirate.\nWhy is it so hard to believe that Sovy might have that moment?
column6: 我不知道，瓦莱莎。我觉得每个人都该有第二次机会。\n我们都有过与三人执政团反目的那个“时刻”。\n为什么就这么难相信索维也可能有那个时刻呢？

column5: He worked so closely with them, he's seen their true nature.\nHe has more knowledge on them than anybody else in our army.\nIt makes sense that he'd come to the same realization as us.
column6: 他曾与他们共事得如此密切，见识过他们的真正本性。\n他对他们的了解比我们军队里任何人都多。\n他会和我们一样得出相同结论，这很合理。

column5: I mean sure, it took a while longer. But that's because he {i}served{/i} them.\nWhen you remove the excuse of \"loyalty\", it can become pretty clear.\nThat's why he didn't fully realize things until they put him in exile.
column6: 我是说，确实花了更长时间。但那是因为他曾在{i}效忠{/i}他们。\n当你抛开“忠诚”这个借口，一切就会变得相当清楚。\n所以直到他们把他流放，他才彻底看清了真相。

column5: Yeah, I'm with Fortaime...! Everybody deserves a second chance.\nWe've all been there before. We've all made a wrong decision or two.\nAnd there's no better way to make up for it than doing the right thing.
column6: 对，我站福泰姆这边……！每个人都该有第二次机会。\n我们都经历过那种时候。我们都做过一两次错误的决定。\n而弥补它的最好方式，莫过于去做正确的事。

column5: Sovy isn't concerned with doing the \"right thing\".\nHe's a liar, plain and simple. There's no way we can trust him.\nHe'd turn on us the moment we arrived in Balteus. That's a guarantee.
column6: 索维根本不在乎做“正确的事”。\n他是个骗子，就这么简单。我们绝不可能信任他。\n我们一到巴尔泰乌斯，他就会反咬我们。这是板上钉钉的。

column5: Letting him close to us now would only enable him to gather information.\nIf he knows our strategy, he can counter is with The Inquisition when we arrive.\nIt's a death sentence, [firstname]. Don't be foolish. We've come too far to risk this.
column6: 现在让他靠近我们，只会让他得以收集情报。\n如果他知道我们的战略，等我们抵达时，他就能协同审判庭反制我们。\n这是死路一条，[firstname]。别犯傻。我们走到这一步太不容易，不能冒这个险。

column5: It seems like my comrades are divided, but with good reason.{w}\nI was hoping for something more unanimous, in any given direction.{w}\nIt was clear that now the pressure, and final decision, rested on my shoulders.
column6: 我的同伴们似乎分成了两派，但都有各自的道理。{w}\n我本希望无论哪个方向，大家都能更一致一些。{w}\n显然，现在压力和最终决定都压在了我的肩上。

column5: Well, [firstname]...?
column6: 那么，[firstname]……？

column5: It was a risk that I was willing to take, for our cause.{w}\nThe information he could offer us would make us so much stronger.{w}\nIf we got suspicious of him before the attack, we could easily outnumber him.
column6: 为了我们的事业，我愿意冒这个险。{w}\n他能提供的情报会让我们强大得多。{w}\n如果我们在进攻前对他起疑，我们能轻易压制他。

column5: There was no way that I could take such a risk.{w}\nIf he turned against us, he could destroy our entire cause.{w}\nIt was too risky. If his exile was even real, he'd be stuck with it.
column6: 我不可能冒这样的险。{w}\n如果他背叛我们，他可能毁掉我们整个事业。{w}\n太冒险了。就算他的流放是真的，那也是他自作自受。

column5: Very well.
column6: 好吧。

column5: He takes a few steps back, and rests against the edge of the boat.{w}\nA few minutes later, after everything is said and done, we arrive in Mazeo.{w}\nThe docking process is short, since our Pirate allies are masters of the art.
column6: 他后退几步，靠在船舷上。{w}\n几分钟后，一切尘埃落定，我们抵达了马泽奥。{w}\n靠岸过程很短暂，因为我们的海盗盟友是此道高手。

column5: Damek steps forward, filling in the silence that overtook our ranks.
column6: 达梅克上前一步，打破了笼罩在我们队伍中的沉默。

column5: Well, this is it — we're ready to attack Balteus.\nEverything we've ever wanted, is finally within our grasp.\nThe voyage will take a day or two, so we can plan on the way.
column6: 好了，就是这样——我们准备好进攻巴尔泰乌斯了。\n我们一直渴望的一切，终于近在咫尺。\n航程要一两天，我们可以在路上筹划。

column5: For now, we need ensure that we leave {i}no{/i} stone unturned.\nVisit with your loved ones, say your goodbyes — because this is it.\nOnce we leave for Balteus, our fates are as good as sealed.
column6: 眼下，我们要确保{i}不{/i}留下任何遗漏。\n去看看你们所爱的人，道别吧——因为就是现在了。\n一旦我们出发前往巴尔泰乌斯，我们的命运就几乎已成定局。

column5: Howl steps forward, filling in the silence that overtook our ranks.
column6: 豪尔上前一步，打破了笼罩在我们队伍中的沉默。

column5: Finally, we're ready to attack Balteus.\nThe liberation of Alestia is at least within our reach.\nBalteus is a few days away by sea, so we can plan on the way.
column6: 终于，我们准备好进攻巴尔泰乌斯了。\n阿莱斯蒂亚的解放至少已触手可及。\n走海路到巴尔泰乌斯要几天，我们可以在路上筹划。

column5: Right now, the preparation you must focus on is that of a goodbye.\nSpend time with your friends, your loved ones — because this is the end.\nOnce we set sail for Balteus, we may never come back. A hard fact to face.
column6: 眼下你必须专注准备的，是一场告别。\n去陪陪你的朋友、你爱的人——因为这就是终局了。\n一旦我们起航前往巴尔泰乌斯，或许就再也回不来了。这是难以面对的事实。

column5: His words are true, but fill the air with tension.{w}\nThe dawn of our final battle was here, and we needed to prepare.{w}\nBut planning the attack was easy. Our true task was accepting our possible death.
column6: 他的话不假，却让空气里充满紧张。{w}\n决战的黎明已经到来，我们必须做好准备。{w}\n但筹划进攻是容易的。真正艰难的任务，是接受自己可能战死。

column5: This means saying goodbye, and spending a final day or two with our friends.{w}\nI should use this opportunity to make sure everybody is prepared for the final battle.{w}\nAs the leader, it was my job to ensure that we were all up to the task. No matter what.
column6: 这意味着道别，意味着和朋友们度过最后的一两天。{w}\n我该利用这个机会，确保每个人都为决战做好了准备。{w}\n作为领袖，我的职责就是确保我们都能胜任这项任务。无论如何。

column5: I don't think there's anything left to say.\nFinish up your business, and we'll set sail when [firstname] demands it.\nAct under the assumption that you only have one or two days before departure.
column6: 我想没什么好说的了。\n把你的私事处理完，等[firstname]下令我们就起航。\n请按只剩一两天就要出发来安排。

column5: I don't want to rush anything as important as a goodbye, but...\nEvery moment we waste is a moment for our enemy to prepare.\nI trust that we'll find a happy medium, and embark without regret.
column6: 我不想催促任何像告别这样重要的事，但是……\n我们浪费的每一刻，都是敌人用来准备的一刻。\n我相信我们会找到折中的办法，不留遗憾地启程。

column5: Everybody nods, agreeing with his words.{w}\nI can't believe that the time was finally here.{w}\nUntil now, it seemed like a dream, out of reach.
column6: 所有人都点头，赞同他的话。{w}\n我不敢相信这一刻终于到来了。{w}\n在那之前，它就像一个遥不可及的梦。

column5: But it's right in front of me. This is it.{w}\nOur journey was in its final hours. I tense up with worry.{w}\nWe make our way off the boat, embracing what little time we had left.
column6: 但它就在我眼前。就是现在了。{w}\n我们的旅程进入了最后的时刻。我紧张得绷紧了神经。{w}\n我们走下船，拥抱我们所剩无几的时光。

column5: Loyalty scenes are now available for the six main party members.{w}\nHowl has a fourth Heart-to-Heart that is hidden in one of the previous areas.{w}\nLoyalty scenes can be accessed by clicking the character icon on the War Table.
column6: 六名主要队员的忠诚剧情现已开放。{w}\n豪尔还有一场隐藏在前述某个区域里的第四次心灵交汇。{w}\n点击作战桌上的角色图标即可进入忠诚剧情。

column5: Fast Travel has now been unlocked, allowing easy navigation through Alestia.{w}\nA new blue icon has appeared in the top left of areas. Click it to move to the World Map.{w}\nThe World Map allows for easy navigation between every other map in the game.
column6: 快速旅行现已解锁，可轻松穿梭阿拉斯蒂亚。{w}\n各区域左上角出现了新的蓝色图标。点击它即可前往世界地图。{w}\n世界地图可让你在游戏中的其他所有地图间轻松移动。

column5: The World Map is also how you will launch your final attack on Balteus.{w}\nClicking the Balteus map icon will give you the choice of entering Act Five.{w}\nHowever, it is best to do this only once you're satisfied with the content you've done.
column6: 世界地图也是你发动对巴尔泰乌斯最终进攻的方式。{w}\n点击巴尔泰乌斯的地图图标，你将可以选择进入第五幕。{w}\n不过，最好等你对已完成的内容满意之后再这么做。

column5: Sovy has now permanently joined your party.{w}\nA series of Heart-to-Hearts has been hidden all over Alestia.{w}\nA loyalty scene has been added, accessed like normal from the War Table.
column6: 索维现已永久加入你的队伍。{w}\n一系列心灵交汇已隐藏在阿拉斯蒂亚各处。{w}\n新增了一场忠诚剧情，照常从作战桌进入。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: It's interesting, to say the least.\nIt's a lot... busier than I thought it would be.\nIt makes Valinorth look dead by comparison.
column6: 至少可以说，这很有趣。\n比我预想的要……热闹得多。\n相比之下，瓦利诺斯简直死气沉沉。

column5: I'm actually longing for that peace again, though.\nThis place is chaotic, there's so much going on.\nHopefully The Rebel HQ will be a bit like home.
column6: 不过我其实已经开始怀念那份宁静了。\n这地方乱糟糟的，事情太多了。\n希望反抗军总部能有点像家的感觉。

column5: He seems to know what he's doing.\nI mean, I had some doubts going into this, actually.\nBut he's proven himself to be a capable leader.
column6: 他似乎很懂自己在做什么。\n我是说，其实一开始我还有些怀疑。\n但他证明了自己是个有能力的领袖。

column5: I like how charismatic he is, you know?\nIt's a lot easier to follow somebody like that.\nSome people demand respect. He {i}earns{/i} it.
column6: 我喜欢他那种魅力，你懂吗？\n追随这样的人容易得多。\n有些人强求尊重。而他是{i}赢得{/i}尊重。

column5: To be honest, I'm actually not sure.\nHe seems nice, but I have my doubts.\nThere's just something about him, you know?
column6: 说实话，我其实不太确定。\n他看起来人不错，但我有些疑虑。\n他身上就是有点说不清楚的东西，你懂吗？

column5: It doesn't help that he likes to cheat people.\nThat's probably it. He {i}is{/i} on our side, though.\nSo I doubt we have to worry about him cheating us.
column6: 他还喜欢骗人，这可没帮上忙。\n大概就是这个原因。不过，他{i}确实{/i}站在我们这边。\n所以我想，我们不用担心他骗我们。

column5: He's the strongest person I've ever met.\nI'm sure he'll be protecting us a lot in the future.\nI don't really have anything bad to say about him.
column6: 他是我见过最强的人。\n我相信以后他会经常保护我们。\n我实在没什么关于他的坏话可说。

column5: He can be stern, but he has the best intentions.\nI mean, he has no patience for wasting time.\nHim and Fortaime make an interesting combo.
column6: 他可能很严厉，但出发点是好的。\n我是说，他没耐心浪费时间。\n他和福泰姆是很有意思的组合。

column5: Pretty good, actually. I was worried.\nYou know, about some of the choices you had to make.\nWe've never really let them get between us, though.
column6: 其实挺好的。我原本很担心。\n你知道的，担心你不得不做出的一些选择。\n不过我们从来没让它们离间过我们。

column5: Unless there's something he's not telling me. But I doubt it.\nHe's always been fully open with me in the past.\nI wouldn't worry about anything at all, [firstname].
column6: 除非他有什么事瞒着我。但我不这么认为。\n过去他一直对我完全坦率。\n我一点都不会担心，[firstname]。

column5: Unless there's something he's not telling me. But I doubt it.\nHe's always been fully open with me in the past.\nI wouldn't worry about anything at all, [firstname].
column6: 除非他有什么事瞒着我。但我不这么认为。\n过去他一直对我完全坦率。\n我一点都不会担心，[firstname]。

column5: There's a massive ship docked, surrounded by workers.{w}\nThey don't seem to be dressed as pirates though.{w}\nMust be part of the Mazeo Shipping Company.
column6: 一艘巨船停靠在码头，四周都是工人。{w}\n不过他们看起来并不像海盗打扮。{w}\n一定是马泽奥航运公司的人。

column5: Wow, that ship is so cool!\nWill our ships be like that, Damek?
column6: 哇，那艘船好酷！\n我们的船也会像那样吗，达梅克？

column5: Of course.\nWe have only the best.\nActually, ours might be better.
column6: 当然。\n我们只用最好的。\n其实，我们的可能还要更好。

column5: Why is that...?
column6: 为什么呢……？

column5: Pirates put more care into their ships.\nThey don't just work on them, they {i}live{/i} on them.\nThe other people have homes to go back to.
column6: 海盗对自己的船更用心。\n他们不只是在船上干活，他们{i}生活{/i}在船上。\n其他人还有家可回。

column5: So pirates are homeless...?
column6: 所以海盗都无家可归……？

column5: Well, not exactly.\nA ship still counts as a home.\nThey just share it with their crew.
column6: 嗯，也不尽然。\n船也算是一个家。\n只是他们得和船员共享。

column5: Oh, I guess that makes sense.\nSo ours will be even fancier than that...?\nThat's pretty hard to imagine. I'm excited.
column6: 哦，我想这说得通。\n那我们的船会比那还要气派……？\n那可真是难以想象。我好兴奋。

column5: Yeah, just be {i}very{/i} careful.\nPirates are super protective of their homes.\nIf you broke something, well — let's not think about that.
column6: 对，不过要{i}非常{/i}小心。\n海盗对自己的家可是保护得紧。\n要是你弄坏了什么，嗯——还是别想这个了。

column5: Yikes.
column6: 哎呀。

column5: What are these...?
column6: 这些是什么……？

column5: Traps.
column6: 陷阱。

column5: Traps for what?
column6: 抓什么的陷阱？

column5: Seafood.
column6: 海鲜。

column5: Oh. We don't have that back in Valinorth.\nHow do these things work, exactly?
column6: 哦。我们在瓦利诺斯没有这种东西。\n这些东西具体是怎么运作的？

column5: Well, these ones are mainly for lobster.\nIt traps them inside, and they're emptied out every day.\nOnce a week, they're sold off in the market square for food.
column6: 嗯，这些主要是用来捕龙虾的。\n它们把龙虾困在里面，每天清空一次。\n每周一次，拿到集市广场上卖掉当食物。

column5: So you capture them only to eat them...?
column6: 所以你们抓它们就是为了吃……？

column5: Yeah.
column6: 对。

column5: I don't know how I feel about that...\nThey're just minding their own business down there.\nWhy should we snatch them up and kill them just like that?
column6: 我不知道该怎么看待这件事……\n它们在下面过着自己的日子，又没招惹谁。\n我们凭什么就这样把它们抓上来杀掉？

column5: Because they taste good.
column6: 因为它们好吃。

column5: There's a bunch of houses lining the docks. They look fancy.{w}\nWorkers come and go, telling me that it's a place of business.{w}\nNear the back, I notice that the houses are more run down.
column6: 码头边排着一列房屋，看起来很气派。{w}\n工人们来来往往，说明这里是做生意的地儿。{w}\n靠近后巷的地方，我注意到那些房子破败得多。

column5: Pirates move back and forth between these houses.{w}\nI guess society only left them the scraps to work with.{w}\nHopefully things would be better for them soon.
column6: 海盗们在这些房屋之间来回穿梭。{w}\n我猜社会只留给他们这些残破的地方。{w}\n希望他们的处境很快就会好起来。

column5: There's a massive bridge on the other side of the docks.{w}\nAccording to Damek, that's the bridge we'd be traversing.{w}\nAt the other end of the bridge, I can see an old building.
column6: 码头另一侧有一座巨大的桥。{w}\n据达梅克说，那就是我们要走的桥。{w}\n在桥的另一端，我能看见一栋老旧的建筑。

column5: Looks pretty impressive, doesn't it?\nMazeo is largely above water, so bridges are common.\nBut there's a couple main bridges. Architectural wonders.
column6: 看起来相当壮观，是吧？\n马泽奥大部分都在水面上，所以桥很常见。\n但有几座主桥。堪称建筑奇迹。

column5: We'll actually be crossing Mazeo's {i}biggest{/i} bridge.\nI hope you're not scared of heights, [firstname].
column6: 我们会走过马泽奥{i}最大的{/i}那座桥。\n希望你不恐高，[firstname]。

column5: We'll actually be crossing Mazeo's {i}biggest{/i} bridge.\nI hope you're not scared of heights, [firstname].
column6: 我们会走过马泽奥{i}最大的{/i}那座桥。\n希望你不恐高，[firstname]。

column5: He smiles and motions toward the very bridge I was inspecting.
column6: 他微笑着，朝我正在打量的一座桥示意。

column5: Our church is just on the other side.\nI can't wait for you to see it. It's amazing.\nJust stick close to me. It won't be too long.
column6: 我们的教堂就在对岸。\n我迫不及待想让你看看。它非常棒。\n就跟紧我。不会用太久。

column5: Sovy and his crew wandered the crowded docks of Mazeo.{w}\nThey stuck close together, to ensure that Shane didn't run away.{w}\nClose to The Rebellion's home, Sovy was sure it crossed his mind.
column6: 索维和他的手下在拥挤的马泽奥码头漫步。{w}\n他们紧紧靠在一起，确保肖恩没有逃走。{w}\n这里离反抗军的据点很近，索维确信他动过这个念头。

column5: Well, you sure seem a lot happier.\nBack on the boat, all you did was mope around.
column6: 嗯，你看起来确实高兴多了。\n在船上的时候，你只会闷闷不乐地晃来晃去。

column5: Sovy scoffed, turning to face his Apprentice.
column6: 索维嗤笑一声，转身面对他的学徒。

column5: Seasickness, I suppose.\nAs old as I am, I've never really gotten used to it.
column6: 大概是晕船吧。\n我年纪这么大了，却始终没真正习惯。

column5: You can't be too much older than me.
column6: 你也不可能比我大多少。

column5: Right, sorry.
column6: 对，抱歉。

column5: Besides, I think I know what's going on.\nYou realized something about The Triumvirate.
column6: 再说，我想我知道是怎么回事。\n你是对三人执政团有所醒悟了。

column5: Yes, I did.\nI see through their trick now.\nIt was a good idea — I'll give them that.
column6: 是的，没错。\n我现在看穿了他们的把戏。\n这主意不错——这我承认。

column5: Trick...?
column6: 把戏……？

column5: Yes. To put my loyalty to the test.\nThere's no way what they told me was true.\nThey merely want to see if I'll waver.
column6: 是的。为了考验我的忠诚。\n他们告诉我的绝不可能是真的。\n他们只是想看看我会不会动摇。

column5: I see...
column6: 原来如此……

column5: That's why they wouldn't tell you, either.\nThis was a test, meant only for {i}me{/i}.
column6: 所以他们也不会告诉你。\n这是一场考验，只针对{i}我{/i}一个人。

column5: So what happens now that you've passed?
column6: 那你通过了，接下来会怎样？

column5: I guess I'll find out once we return.\nI'm just glad that I can focus on the mission now.
column6: 我想等我们回去就知道了。\n我只是很高兴现在能专心执行任务了。

column5: Right. I'm glad too, I suppose.\nOn the boat, you were in no condition to perform.
column6: 对。我想我也很高兴。\n在船上时，你根本没法做事。

column5: After a few more minutes of walking, Sovy stops in his tracks.{w}\nHalin and Shane bump into his back, causing him to stumble over.
column6: 又走了几分钟后，索维停下了脚步。{w}\n哈林和肖恩撞上他的后背，让他踉跄了一下。

column5: Master...?
column6: 主人……？

column5: Oh, sorry. Just a lot on my mind.
column6: 哦，抱歉。只是心事太多。

column5: We're not lost, are we...?
column6: 我们没迷路吧……？

column5: Sovy stares at a cloaked figure in the distance.{w}\nHe smirks as he watches them walk through the docks with a group.{w}\nA large item affixed to their back sways with each of their heavy steps.
column6: 索维盯着远处一个披斗篷的身影。{w}\n他看着那人随一群人穿过码头，嘴角泛起笑意。{w}\n一件系在他们背后的巨大物件随着每一步沉重的脚步摇摆。

column5: No. Not at all...
column6: 不。一点也没有……

column5: I make my way to the ship, as Damek instructed.{w}\nEveryone is already gathered around. Am I late?{w}\nBefore long, I'm spotted by a few of my friends.
column6: 我按照达梅克的吩咐前往那艘船。{w}\n所有人都已经聚在周围了。我来晚了吗？{w}\n没过多久，就有几个朋友发现了我。

column5: Hey there, [firstname]!\nGlad to see you made it on time.\nThey're just about ready to leave Mazeo.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]！\n很高兴看到你准时赶到了。\n他们马上就要离开马泽奥了。

column5: I'm so excited to see what Alarinthia is like.\nI mean — except for the heat, of course. Yikes.\nBut I guess there'll be plenty of time to adapt.
column6: 我太期待看看阿拉林西亚是什么样子了。\n我是说——当然，除了那酷热之外。哎哟。\n不过我想总有足够的时间适应。

column5: Yeah, I don't think our visit there will be a short one.\nIt's kind of a tall order, forming an alliance with Alarinthia.\nThey take their independence seriously. Even more than Valinorth.
column6: 是啊，我觉得我们去那儿不会是短住。\n和阿拉林西亚结盟可是件难事。\n他们很看重独立。甚至比瓦利诺斯更甚。

column5: I think that Vivien will be our best shot.\nBut I trust you and Damek to get this done.\nYou're a dream team, so this {i}has{/i} to go well.
column6: 我觉得薇薇安会是我们最好的突破口。\n但我相信你和达梅克能办成这件事。\n你们是梦幻组合，所以这{i}一定{/i}会顺利。

column5: Upon hearing his name, Damek's ears perk up.{w}\nHe turns around and runs to face me — excited.{w}\nI'm impressed at how fast he organized this.
column6: 听到自己的名字，达梅克的耳朵竖了起来。{w}\n他转过身，兴冲冲地跑向我。{w}\n我对他组织得如此之快感到佩服。

column5: [firstname]! Perfect timing, as always.\nI was just telling my friends about you.\nHere, let me introduce you to some of them.
column6: [firstname]！一如既往地恰到好处。\n我刚在跟我的朋友们说起你。\n来，让我给你介绍几位。

column5: He starts walking away, leading me to some nearby rebels.{w}\nI've never seen them before, but they're lucky to be alive.{w}\nThe previous attack almost took {i}everybody{/i} from us.
column6: 他开始走开，领我去见附近的一些反抗军。{w}\n我从没见过他们，但他们能活下来真是幸运。{w}\n上一次袭击差点让我们失去{i}所有人{/i}。

column5: As your advisor, I have a few close friends.\nThey'll provide me with counsel when you're busy.\nWe both know that's going to be quite often, [firstname].
column6: 作为你的顾问，我有几个亲近的朋友。\n你忙的时候，他们会为我出谋划策。\n我们都知道你忙的时候会很多，[firstname]。

column5: This much was true.
column6: 这话不假。

column5: Everybody, I'd like to introduce you to The Monarch.\nTreat him as you treated me. He's your new leader, now.\nAnd after this war, he'll be the new ruler of Alestia.
column6: 各位，我想向你们介绍君主。\n你们怎么对待我，就怎么对待他。他现在是你们的新领袖。\n这场战争之后，他将成为阿莱斯蒂亚的新统治者。

column5: Everybody, I'd like to introduce you to The Monarch.\nTreat her as you treated me. She's your new leader, now.\nAnd after this war, she'll be the new ruler of Alestia.
column6: 各位，我想向你们介绍君主。\n你们怎么对待我，就怎么对待她。她现在是你们的新领袖。\n这场战争之后，她将成为阿莱斯蒂亚的新统治者。

column5: That was still overwhelming to think about.{w}\nI guess I'll have to take things as they come. One step at a time.{w}\nDamek's friends take turns stepping forward, seemingly nervous.
column6: 光是想想这些，依然让人不知所措。{w}\n我想我只能走一步看一步，一步一步来。{w}\n达梅克的朋友们轮流上前，看起来有些紧张。

column5: I've heard a lot about you, Monarch.\nUntil you arrived, you're all Damek could talk about.\nYou have my allegiance. My sword is yours to command.
column6: 我久仰你的大名，君主。\n你来之前，达梅克满嘴都是你。\n我向你效忠。我的剑听你调遣。

column5: And mine, too! Trust me [firstname], we got this.\nAfter this is done, Alestia will belong to {i}us{/i}.\nAnd if I'm honest — it's about damn time.
column6: 还有我！相信我，[firstname]，这事我们稳了。\n等这一切结束，阿莱斯蒂亚就属于{i}我们{/i}了。\n而且说实话——早该如此了。

column5: Yeah, The Triumvirate has ruled over us for far too long.\nA change is overdue — it'll keep things nice and interesting.\nPlease [firstname], come to me if you need any assistance at all.
column6: 是啊，三人执政团统治我们太久了。\n变革早就该来了——这样才能让一切保持新鲜有趣。\n[firstname]，如果你需要任何帮助，尽管来找我。

column5: As if they rehearsed this, they all step back in unison.{w}\nIt was nice to see that Damek had the support of his rebels.{w}\nThey don't seem to hold him accountable, like Howl did.
column6: 仿佛排练过一样，他们齐刷刷地退后一步。{w}\n很高兴看到达梅克有他的反抗军支持。{w}\n他们似乎不像豪尔那样追究他的责任。

column5: Well, I guess that's everything I needed to do.\nThe food and supplies have all been taken aboard.\nAlex took care of it overnight. I guess he couldn't sleep.
column6: 嗯，我想我要做的都做完了。\n食物和补给都已经装船了。\n亚历克斯熬了一夜把它们办妥。我猜他没睡着。

column5: I don't blame him.
column6: 我不怪他。

column5: Should we continue the rest on the ship?\nThere's still a few people you need to meet.\nAfter that, we're in for a long, boring trip.
column6: 剩下的要不要到船上再说？\n还有几个人你得见一见。\n之后，我们就要踏上漫长又无聊的旅程了。

column5: I nod, and start to follow him aboard.{w}\nEverybody else follows suit, until we're all loaded up.{w}\nThis would be my first time at sea. I hope my body takes it well.
column6: 我点点头，跟着他上了船。{w}\n其他人也依次跟上，直到我们全部登船。{w}\n这将是我第一次出海。希望我的身体能适应。

column5: Well, I guess that's everything I needed to do.\nThe food and supplies have all been taken aboard.\nNada insisted, I guess she couldn't get any sleep.
column6: 嗯，我想我要做的都做完了。\n食物和补给都已经装船了。\n娜达坚持要帮忙，我猜她根本没睡。

column5: I don't blame her.
column6: 我不怪她。

column5: I think that Vivien will be our best shot.\nHopefully you and Howl can get along, [firstname].\nIt's a new partnership, but it certainly shows promise.
column6: 我觉得薇薇安会是我们最好的突破口。\n希望你和豪尔能相处融洽，[firstname]。\n这是段新的合作关系，但显然很有前景。

column5: Upon hearing his \"name\", Howl's ears perk up.{w}\nHe walks toward me, ending his previous conversation.{w}\nI can't believe this was all organized so fast, and so efficiently.
column6: 听到自己的“名字”，豪尔的耳朵竖了起来。{w}\n他结束了先前的谈话，朝我走来。{w}\n我真不敢相信这一切组织得如此之快、如此高效。

column5: [firstname], glad to see that you made it.\nWe were just talking with some new \"supporters\".\nIt appears that our partnership is welcomed by many.
column6: [firstname]，很高兴看到你来了。\n我们刚在和几位新的“支持者”交谈。\n看来我们的结盟受到了许多人的欢迎。

column5: We are not the only ones who hold Damek accountable.\nIf it's okay, we'd like to introduce you to a few of them.\nHopefully, they will solidify your choice as correct.
column6: 不是只有我们才追究达梅克的责任。\n如果可以，我们想给你介绍其中几位。\n希望他们能让你更加确信你的选择是正确的。

column5: I nod, and follow Howl back to where he was before.{w}\nA few rebels stand there, smiling as they see me.{w}\nHowl motions toward them, and I step forward.
column6: 我点点头，跟着豪尔回到他刚才待的地方。{w}\n几个反抗军站在那里，看到我便露出笑容。{w}\n豪尔朝他们示意，我走上前去。

column5: Pleasure to meet you, [firstname].\nI'm glad to see that you survived the attack.\nThanks to Damek, not everybody was so lucky.
column6: 很高兴见到你，[firstname]。\n很高兴你从袭击中活了下来。\n多亏了达梅克，可不是每个人都那么走运。

column5: They told us he was an unparalleled strategist.\nWell, if he is — he lost the chance to prove it to us.\nI gotta say, I'm glad you changed the way things are run.
column6: 他们说他是个无与伦比的战略家。\n嗯，如果真是——那他已经没机会向我们证明了。\n我得说，我很高兴你改变了这里的行事方式。

column5: Yeah. Howl seems like the perfect choice, [firstname].\nIt's good to know that we're in the hands of somebody wise.\nUnder your command — we'll recover from this — and win.
column6: 是啊。豪尔似乎是最合适的人选，[firstname]。\n知道自己掌握在明智之人的手里真好。\n在你的指挥下——我们会恢复过来——然后赢。

column5: They all step away, and go about their business.{w}\nSo there {i}are{/i} other rebels who think Damek is responsible.{w}\nThat means there are others that support Damek. I hope this is okay.
column6: 他们全都退开，各忙各的去了。{w}\n所以{i}确实{/i}有别的反抗军认为达梅克该负责。{w}\n那就意味着也有人支持达梅克。希望这没关系。

column5: Conflict is the last thing we need among our own forces.{w}\nIt would definitely hinder our morale in the coming storm.{w}\nI turn back to Howl, who seems happy and relaxed.
column6: 冲突是我们自己人之间最不需要的东西。{w}\n在即将到来的风暴中，那肯定会打击我们的士气。{w}\n我转回豪尔那边，他看起来愉快又放松。

column5: We should probably get going, [firstname].\nEverything is on the ship, and everybody is here.\nAlex worked overnight to make sure we were ready.
column6: 我们大概该动身了，[firstname]。\n东西都在船上了，人也到齐了。\n亚历克斯熬了一夜确保我们准备妥当。

column5: Talk about dedication.
column6: 真是尽职尽责。

column5: Shall we continue the rest of this discussion at sea?\nIf anything, it'll help pass the time. Alarinthia is quite far away.\nWe'll take a shipping route used by our people in ancient times.
column6: 剩下的讨论要不要到海上继续？\n至少这样能打发时间。阿拉林西亚可远着呢。\n我们会走我们族人在上古时代用过的航线。

column5: I nod, and start to follow him aboard.{w}\nEverybody else follows suit, until we're all loaded up.{w}\nThis would be my first time at sea. I hope my body takes it well.
column6: 我点点头，跟着他上了船。{w}\n其他人也依次跟上，直到我们全部登船。{w}\n这将是我第一次出海。希望我的身体能适应。

column5: We should probably get going, Monarch.\nEverything is on the ship, and everybody is here.\nNada worked overnight to make sure we were ready.
column6: 我们大概该动身了，君主。\n东西都在船上了，人也到齐了。\n娜达熬了一夜确保我们准备妥当。

column5: Talk about dedication.
column6: 真是尽职尽责。
